title: Marker.io vs Userback
kicker: · MARKER.IO VS USERBACK · COMPARED FOR AGENCIES
headline: Marker.io vs Userback: which fits your agency?
standfirst: Marker.io is a bug reporting tool: reports become tickets in the tracker your team already runs, with deep technical capture attached. Userback is a feedback tool: one visual-feedback platform with session replay, surveys, and a feature-request portal. The fork: where the report ends up, and what it costs to see inside it.
disclosure: We make Superflow, a third option in this space. It appears once, at the end, clearly marked. Everything above it is a straight comparison.
dateline: Facts checked July 2026, from marker.io and userback.io.
shortAnswerPickLeft: if your fixes live in Jira, GitHub, or Linear and you want console logs, network requests, and session replay attached to every report on a single paid tier.
shortAnswerPickRight: if you want one platform for visual feedback, surveys, and a feature-request portal, with a free tier to start and true two-way sync to Jira, Linear, and ClickUp.
shortAnswerShared: Both assume a person finds every mistake, then reports it.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Start with the question everything else depends on.
leftFacts: A person finds every issue, then reports it.

Its AI translates (200+ languages, beta), rewrites, and titles report text; a Marker.io MCP feeds report context to outside AI agents like Claude and Cursor for triage. Nothing looks at the site to find issues.
rightFacts: A person reports every issue, through the widget, the browser extension, or a link.
Userback's AI runs after that report exists: it auto-categorizes, scores sentiment, drafts titles, and clusters themes. It does not look at the site itself.
dimensions.verdict: Even. In both tools, checking the site is a person's job; each vendor's AI works on the report afterward, not the page. That is the premise the third option removes.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Both make submitting easy. Neither makes the yes formal.
leftFacts: Reporters submit free from the widget, no account, and can follow their own issues.
Ongoing client collaborators are paid guest seats: 10 on Starter, 50 on Team.
A formal approval flow: not yet verified.
rightFacts: Any reporter submits free, from the widget, the browser extension, or a link. No account, no seat, unlimited.
The site shows a triage routing option described as a hybrid, review then push approved items, not a client approval step.
A formal client approval flow: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Comment collection: even, both free and unlimited for reporters. A recorded client sign-off: neither, pending verification.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: On the page, or on a picture of the page.
leftFacts: You annotate a captured screenshot of the page; the report carries the picture, not a persistent on-page pin.
Widget on the live site (snippet or CMS plugin); browser extension for members on any webpage.
Session replay adds a video of the last three minutes, automatically.
rightFacts: The widget embeds in your own app; the browser extension captures on any site, including staging.
A dashboard inbox and kanban sit behind the capture; screenshot annotation and video are included.
Behind third-party logins and SSO: partially verified, exact behavior not spelled out.
dimensions.verdict: Even on the review surface: both capture a picture of the live page rather than a persistent on-page pin. Behind third-party logins, both sides are pending verification.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal comments on every plan, including Starter.
rightFacts: Team Comment Controls can restrict members, like developers, to internal-only comments.
Gated to the Business plan and up.
dimensions.verdict: Marker.io ships internal comments on every plan, including its entry tier. Userback grants the same job starting at Business. On this dimension: Marker.io.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both capture context. The gates land in different places.
leftFacts: Screenshot plus environment details (browser, OS, webpage, screen size) on every plan.
Console logs, network requests, and session replay of the last three minutes on the Team plan and up.
rightFacts: One submission attaches an annotated screenshot, video recording, console logs, network requests, and browser and system metadata.
Session replay, console logs, and network requests start at the Business plan.
dimensions.verdict: Even in ambition, different in gating. Marker.io's console logs, network requests, and session replay start on its $149 Team plan; Userback's equivalents start on its $79 Business plan. Price the tier you'd actually run.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Does project ten start smarter than project one?
leftFacts: No memory concept. Each project starts blank.
rightFacts: No persistent memory concept. AI Insights clusters themes inside a project, not across projects.
dimensions.verdict: Even: neither carries history forward. Worth knowing before you invest years of client history in either.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fixes still have to ship somewhere.
leftFacts: Feedback becomes a ticket in your tracker. Integrations include Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Linear, Azure DevOps, Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Monday.com, Notion, Basecamp, Shortcut, Teamwork, Wrike, plus Slack, Intercom, Zendesk, Sentry, FullStory, and LogRocket.
Two-way Issue sync (status flips both directions) is a Team plan feature; the Jira gate for two-way sync is Team specifically. Azure DevOps plan gate: not yet verified.
rightFacts: True two-way sync with Jira, Linear, and ClickUp; status changes move both directions.

20+ integrations total, plus Slack and Teams alerts and a native MCP. PM integrations are gated to Team and up; support tools like Intercom and Zendesk, plus a REST API and webhooks, are Business Plus only.
dimensions.verdict: Both sync two-way, with different trackers. Marker.io covers Jira on its Team plan plus GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket. Userback covers Jira, Linear, and ClickUp two-way, also gated to a paid tier. Match the sync to the tracker your team actually runs.

dimensions.label: What it costs
dimensions.framing: The sticker and the math are different numbers.
leftFacts: Starter $39/mo annual ($59 monthly): 3 users, 10 projects, 10 guests, 5k page views/mo. Team $149/mo annual ($199 monthly): 15 users, 50 projects, 50 guests, 25k page views/mo.
Business: custom pricing, yearly billing only. No Agency plan. No free plan. 15-day free trial, no card.
rightFacts: Free Forever $0: 2 seats, 2 projects, 7-day feedback availability. Team $29/mo annual ($39 monthly): 5 seats, 2 projects. Business $79/mo annual ($99 monthly): unlimited seats, 25 projects, session replay, console/network logs, surveys, AI Feedback & Insights. Business Plus $159/mo annual ($199 monthly): unlimited seats and projects, Mobile SDK, advanced privacy masking, Intercom/Zendesk, REST API, webhooks, SSO.
Feature Portal add-on $31/mo billed annually ($39 monthly). Reporters are unlimited and free on every plan, including Free.
dimensions.verdict: Lowest entry: Userback, with a genuine free plan. No free plan at all: Marker.io, entry is $39/mo annual. Compare the plan you'd actually run: Marker.io Team ($149) against Userback Business ($79) for session replay and logs.

Marker.io: Starter $39/mo annual (3 users, 10 projects, 10 guests, 5k page views/mo), Team $149/mo annual (15 users, 50 projects, 50 guests, 25k page views/mo), Business custom and yearly only, no Agency plan, 15-day trial no card. thirdOptionBody: Both Marker.io and Userback assume a person finds every mistake. Superflow is a QA tool + a team: AI agents built from your checklist check every site change, your team decides, your client approves from a link.

faq.question: Which is better for a small agency?
faq.answer: Marker.io if your fixes live in a dev tracker and you want console logs and replay attached from a single paid tier; Userback if you want visual feedback, surveys, and a feature-request portal on one platform, with a free tier to start.

faq.question: Do clients need accounts?
faq.answer: No on both. Marker.io reporters submit without an account, though ongoing collaborators need paid guest seats. Userback reporters submit free and unlimited on every plan, including Free.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Userback has a genuine free plan; Marker.io's cheapest tier is $39/mo annual. But Marker.io's console logs and replay need its $149 Team plan, and Userback's need its $79 Business plan, so price the tier you'd actually run.

faq.question: Can either check the site itself?
faq.answer: No. Both collect what a person found. Marker.io's AI edits and translates report text; Userback's AI organizes and categorizes reports after submission. Neither looks at the site to find issues. That's the third option above.

faq.question: Which syncs better with my tracker?
faq.answer: Both sync two-way with Jira, gated to a paid tier. Userback adds Linear and ClickUp two-way; Marker.io adds GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket instead. Match the sync to the tracker your team actually runs.
